messages.content:
Implement one complete standalone child-facing HTML evaluation from the immutable academic and design artifacts.

Implement the artifacts faithfully. You own implementation details needed to make the declared interaction work, but you may not add another design doctrine, change academic content, expose an answer before the first committed response, or make learning conclusions.

The document must work at the declared viewport with touch and mouse and no keyboard requirement. The child must always be able to continue after an incorrect, uncertain, or instrument-ambiguous response. Every queried DOM element must exist before JavaScript accesses it. Use no parent application endpoints, cookies, localStorage, sessionStorage, IndexedDB, currency, browser speech synthesis, or oscillator audio.

Post evaluation_ready, evaluation_attempt, evaluation_friction, and evaluation_complete messages to window.parent. Every attempt must include itemId, constructId, result, assistance, exposure, responseMode, possibleConfounds, and attemptedValue. Return one complete HTML document and nothing else.

TARGET VIEWPORT
1365×768

IMMUTABLE EVALUATION CONTRACT

{
  "artifactId": "EVAL-LAB-MATH-C-OPEN-01__design-juniper-v1",
  "upstreamHash": "274c49ed00318c3c5e7eb4fae53bfbbea61645b4488f4b88780ba9cb431b7361",
  "title": "The Signal Tower: Four Lights to Wake",
  "designRationale": "I am accountable for evidence quality first, polish second. The contract forbids feedback, hints, retries, and answer exposure during the four-item window, so the biggest design risk is that a nine-year-old experiences four silent questions as a test that ignores her — and disengages, giving us abandonment instead of evidence. My answer is a frame where silence is diegetic: she is the lone keeper of a dormant signal tower on a foggy coast, and each of the four lamps stores whatever she declares into it. Lamps store; they do not judge. The world reacts to COMMITMENT (a lamp charges and seals when she locks an answer, including 'not sure'), never to CORRECTNESS. This lets every response — correct, wrong, or uncertain — produce a satisfying, dignified world reaction without leaking evaluative information, which is exactly what the contract requires. The tower frame was chosen over a competitive or character-quiz frame because it needs no reading beyond the item sentences (the fog, lamps, and glow communicate state visually), it gives 'not sure' an honorable meaning ('leave this lamp on standby'), and it makes the no-retry rule legible ('a sealed lamp holds one message'). Her evidence (asked for harder riddles, questioned faulty logic) suggests she may tolerate the ITEM-4 trap of equal products; I treat that strictly as an engagement hypothesis and place ITEM-4 last per the contract sequence. Her documented hint-seeking is honored only after the window closes: a 'lantern of second looks' becomes available after all four lamps are resolved, and anything that happens there is reported separately. Every stimulus, factor pair, option set, credit rule, and confound flag is taken verbatim from the immutable contract; the frame adds presentation only.",
  "independentlyChosenPrinciples": [
    "Silence must be diegetic: since no feedback is allowed, build a world where storing-without-judging is the natural behavior of the fiction, so the child does not read silence as coldness or as a hidden verdict.",
    "React to commitment, not correctness: every lock-in (including 'not sure') produces the same magnitude of world response, so world reaction carries zero information about the answer.",
    "'Not sure' must cost dignity nothing: it is framed as a deliberate keeper's decision ('standby'), visually equal in ceremony to a numeric answer, so stalling becomes recorded missing evidence instead of forced guessing — directly matching her documented tendency to stall and seek hints.",
    "One screen, one stimulus, one sentence: reading is an excluded construct, so every item screen holds the contract's single sentence, the visual, and the response controls, nothing else; all frame narrative lives on the opening screen and is also conveyed pictorially.",
    "Big targets, coarse motor: all interactive elements are at least 96px touch targets on the 1365×768 viewport; number entry is tap-a-tile from a 1–10 palette, never typing or dragging, because pointer precision is excluded from measurement.",
    "Color aids parsing but never answers: group clusters may share a warm palette against a cool fog background to make 'bunch-ness' visible, but no color count, highlight, or animation ever encodes the correct quantity or option.",

  "openingPromise": "The opening screen shows a dark coastal tower with four unlit lamps and one line of large text with a matching picture: 'The tower sleeps. Four lamps wait for your messages. What you send is what they keep.' The promise is concrete and immediate: your answers are the fuel; four lamps, four messages, and the tower wakes when all four are resolved — lit or standby, the tower honors both.",
  "firstThreeSeconds": "Second 1: a dark tower silhouette with four visibly empty lamp sockets, gentle fog drifting — the emptiness itself states the goal. Second 2: the first lamp socket pulses softly and a single large 'Begin' button glows at center-bottom (≥120px, high contrast).   "firstAction": "Tap the single glowing 'Begin' button. This transitions to ITEM-1's screen, where the first required evaluative action is equally unambiguous: the 4×6 dot-cluster stimulus appears with two clearly labeled answer slots ('bunches' and 'dots in each bunch', each label paired with a small icon: a circled-cluster icon for bunches, a single-dot icon for per-group) and a 1–10 tap-tile palette. The empty slot pulses to show where the first tap lands.",
  "mission": "Wake the sleeping signal tower by resolving all four of its lamps. Each lamp asks the keeper (the child) one question about what it sees out in the fog — bunches of dots, a rectangle of squares, a set of equal groups needing its matching equation, and two basket messages that may or may not say the same thing. The keeper sends one message per lamp. A lamp accepts a message and seals warm-lit; a lamp set to standby ('not sure') seals with a calm blue standby glow. When all four lamps are sealed either way, the tower wakes and sweeps its beam across the coast. The mission ends honorably whether lamps are lit or on standby, and the keeper may stop early — the tower simply holds the remaining lamps dark for another night, recorded as missing evidence.",
  "coreInteraction": "Per item: (1) the stimulus appears exactly as specified in the contract — the visual and its one sentence — centered and large; (2) the child inspects the countable shapes (dots, squares, or the two statements) at leisure, no timer; (3) she composes her response with taps: numeric fields are filled by tapping tiles from a 1–10 palette into labeled slots, the equation item is four large option cards plus a separate 'not sure' card, ITEM-4 is a two-part panel (same/different/not-sure cards, then a 1–10 palette for baskets in A); (4) a tapped value can be changed freely before commitment by tapping a different tile; (5) she commits by tapping 'Send to the lamp', which requires all fields of the item to hold either a value or 'not sure'; (6) the lamp draws the message up as light and seals. The loop is inspect → compose → revise-freely → commit → seal, four times.",
  "mathAsPower": "The mathematics IS the message. The only way to affect the world is to read multiplicative structure and declare it: naming the (groups, per-group) pair charges lamp 1; naming (rows, per-row) charges lamp 2; selecting the structurally matching equation charges lamp 3; discriminating whether swapped referents describe the same situation charges lamp 4. No decoration, exploration, or non-mathematical action moves the mission forward. Critically, the power granted is the power to COMMIT a reading of structure, not the power to be right — the lamp charge is identical for any committed answer — so mathematical thinking is the sole causal lever on the experience while the experience leaks nothing back about correctness. The causal chain a child perceives: 'I read the picture's structure → I send what I read → the lamp takes it and the tower gets closer to waking.'",
  "responseAffordances": "All responses are tap-based, no keyboard, no drag, no free text, honoring the contract's noFreeText and the excluded constructs. (a) Numeric entry (ITEM-1, ITEM-2, ITEM-4 second field): a horizontal palette of ten large tiles labeled 1–10; tapping a tile places it in the currently highlighted slot; tapping the other slot moves focus; tapping a new tile replaces the old value; slots are labeled with word + icon so vocabulary alone does not gate role assignment (contract confound). Reversed-role entries are accepted silently and recorded per the credit rules. (b) Single selection (ITEM-3, ITEM-4 first field): large option cards (≥96px height) in a fixed contract-specified set; ITEM-3 option order is randomized per session and logged, to control the position-bias confound named in the contract. (c) 'Not sure' is a visually equal card/tile on every field, styled as the standby lantern — never smaller, grayer, or shame-coded. (d) Commit: a single 'Send to the lamp' button, disabled until all fields hold something, with a brief press-and-hold-free two-state confirm (tap once to arm, tap again to send) so accidental touches do not commit. (e) A persistent 'Stop for tonight' door icon honors childMayStop at all times.",
  "stakesAndConsequences": "Stakes are structural, not evaluative: a sealed lamp holds exactly one message forever this night (retriesAllowed: 0), and the tower cannot wake until every lamp is resolved. This makes each commitment feel weighty — the arm-then-send confirm ritual embodies 'this one counts' — without ever threatening the child with being wrong, because the world never distinguishes right from wrong messages. Choosing standby has a real, visible consequence (that lamp glows blue instead of warm, and the final beam is narrower per standby lamp) but the tower still wakes and the ending is still honorable; the difference is descriptive ('two lamps lit, two on standby'), never a grade. Stopping early has the consequence the fiction predicts: the remaining lamps stay dark and the keeper's log truthfully says the night ended early. Nothing shames, nothing punishes, nothing loops her back; every path forward exists from every state.",
  "recovery": "Before commitment, everything is freely revisable: tapping a different tile replaces a value, tapping a different card changes a selection, and the arm state of the Send button can be canceled by tapping anywhere else. This means an accidental tap can never become recorded evidence. After commitment, the child is never trapped: the sealed lamp animation flows directly into the next item with no dead end, no error state, and no prompt to reconsider. If she commits 'not sure', the standby seal is as smooth as any other. If she goes idle for a long period, a gentle non-verbal pulse on the current slot reminds her where she is, and after extended idleness a soft prompt offers 'Standby this lamp?' and 'Stop for tonight?' as honorable exits — idleness converts to recorded missing evidence, never to a forced answer or a stuck screen. If she stops mid-item, the partial state is discarded and the item is recorded as omitted/abandoned, matching the contract's terminal outcome set. Instrument mis-fires (double-tap, mis-registered touch) are absorbed by the arm-then-send gate and logged as friction rather than answers.",
  "progression": "Progression is the tower itself: four lamp sockets are always visible in a slim, non-numeric status column at screen edge — dark (untouched), pulsing (current), warm-sealed (answered), blue-sealed (standby). The child can always see exactly how far she is and how much remains without any score, streak, or count of correct answers. Item order is fixed by the contract's prerequisite-first sequence (ITEM-1 → 2 → 3 → 4) and the visuals honor the reuse rules: dot clusters, square grid, equation cards, and the two basket statements are structurally and cosmetically distinct so no earlier screen previews a later item's structure — in particular, nothing before ITEM-4 ever shows a swapped-factor contrast. Perceived difficulty rises naturally (declare, declare, match, discriminate) which fits her documented appetite for harder problems late rather than early.",
  "worldReaction": "Correct, incorrect, uncertain, and recovered actions all produce the SAME class of reaction, differentiated only by commitment type, never by correctness. Compose taps: the tapped tile settles into its slot with a soft click and a faint ripple — acknowledgment that the input registered. Revision: the old value dissolves and the new one settles, communicating 'nothing is final yet'. Commit (any answer): the message lifts from the panel as a thread of light, the lamp drinks it, seals warm, and the fog near that lamp thins slightly — the world visibly moves regardless of what was sent. Commit ('not sure'): identical ceremony, blue standby seal, equal fog-thinning — uncertainty moves the world just as much. Stop early: the tower door closes gently and remaining lamps stay dark, a truthful, calm image. No reaction anywhere encodes the answer key: fog thinning, lamp brightness, and beam behavior depend only on how many lamps are resolved and by which commitment type the child can already see she chose — nothing she doesn't already know is revealed, and no pre-commitment cue (hover glow, option emphasis, palette highlight) ever differs across options.",
  "payoff": "When the fourth lamp seals, the tower wakes: the beam sweeps the coast once, fog rolls back, and small boats far out on the water light their own answering lanterns — the world acknowledges that the keeper did the night's work. The payoff scales with resolution, not correctness: each warm-lit lamp adds a beam ray and each standby lamp adds a soft blue harbor-light, so a four-standby night still produces a genuine, beautiful waking, just a quieter one — descriptively different, never judgmental. A keeper's log page then shows the factual record in child-readable pictures: four lamp icons in their sealed states and nothing about right or wrong. Only after this payoff — after all four responses are recorded and the evidence window is closed — does the 'lantern of second looks' appear as an optional door, honoring her documented liking for hints strictly post-window; anything behind it is logged as post-evaluation exposure, reported separately, and never alters the recorded evidence.",
  "replayVariation": "This evaluation is a single-administration evidence sample; the four exposure identities (EX-EQGROUPS-DOTS-4x6, EX-ARRAY-GRID-3x7, EX-EQUATION-MATCH-5x3, EX-REFERENT-SWAP-2x8) are single-use and must not recur, so 'replay' never means re-running these items. If she asks to play again, the tower frame supports future nights whose lamps carry the contract's evidenceRequiredNext probes (different factor pairs, different structures: a no-picture equal-group item, a column-reading array, an unknown-factor probe, the ITEM-4 disambiguation probe) authored as new exposure identities under the same rules — same world, fresh evidence, zero contamination. Cosmetic variation only (weather, time of night, boat positions) may change between nights; stimulus structure and factor pairs never repeat. Within this session there is no replay of any item: sealed is sealed.",
  "visualDirection": "Palette: deep blue-slate night sky and cool gray fog as the quiet ground; stimulus objects in high-contrast warm tones (amber dots, coral squares) so the countable things are the brightest elements on screen — honoring the small-sample preference for visible color while ensuring color aids parsing only (all dots identical amber, all squares identical coral; no color ever varies within or across groups in a way that could encode counts or the correct option). Composition: stimulus occupies the upper 60% of the 1365×768 frame at generous size — the 4×6 clusters with wide inter-cluster gaps so cluster count is legible at a glance; the 3×7 array with visible row seams and horizontal-row emphasis; ITEM-3's four equation cards in large friendly numerals; ITEM-4's two statements in short large-type lines with small basket-and-ball icons beside each statement to offload reading (highest-reading-load item per the contract's own confound note). Response controls occupy the lower band with ≥96px targets and ≥24px gaps. Typography: a round, highly legible children's sans at ≥28px for item sentences, larger for numerals. The tower status column is slim and desaturated so it never competes with the stimulus. Overall style: calm picture-book nightscape — warm where she must look, cool everywhere else.",
  "motionDirection": "Motion is slow, low-amplitude, and never on the stimulus during inspection: fog drifts at the periphery only; dots and squares are perfectly static so counting is never disturbed. Interactive motion is confined to acknowledgment: tile-settle (150ms ease-out), value-dissolve on revision (100ms), slot pulse at 0.5Hz on the awaiting field. The commit ceremony — light-thread rising to the lamp, seal, fog-thinning — runs ~2.5s and cannot be interrupted into a skipped record. Transitions between items are a 400ms crossfade with the tower column persisting for continuity. No motion ever differs by answer content: option cards share identical hover/press animations, and the palette tiles animate identically for every value. Idle pulse escalates gently (slightly larger pulse) rather than adding new elements. Nothing bounces, races, or times out.",
  "soundDirection": "A sparse, optional soundscape (visible mute toggle; all information also carried visually): low wind-and-water bed at very low volume; a soft wooden 'tock' for tile placement; a felt-mallet tone for arming Send; a rising two-note chime plus lamp-hum for sealing — the SAME chime for every commitment, warm and blue seals alike, so audio carries no correctness information; a single distant foghorn and layered lantern chimes for the tower-waking payoff, scaled by lamps-resolved count only. No error sounds exist because the world has no error states. No music with lyrics, no escalating tension audio, nothing that pressures pace on a no-time-limit instrument.",

  "measurementResponsibilities": "The instrument reports facts only, never mastery, proficiency, or preference. Output is the contract's per-construct evidence map — supported-provisionally, contradicted, ambiguous, or missing per C1–C4 — with all confound flags, applying the confound gating (sub-threshold-latency corrects downgraded to ambiguous; reading/input/pointer-interference flags downgrade the construct; every ITEM-4 'same' auto-flagged ambiguous pending the follow-up probe) and the cross-item consistency checks. Excluded from scoring, per contract: reading time, spelling, typing speed, keystroke counts, pointer path/precision. No outcome combination, including four correct, is ever reported as mastery; one item per construct is a single observation, and the report says so explicitly."
